title: Supplier Residual Data Erasure & Certification Template
content:
Purpose:
This template defines Supplier obligations to securely erase residual customer data following termination, suspension, or as otherwise requested by Customer, and to provide a verifiable certification of erasure. It is intended for inclusion as a contract schedule or annex to data processing agreements, managed service agreements, or supplier security addenda.

Scope:
Applies to all Customer Data (defined below) that Supplier stores, processes, caches, or otherwise holds directly or indirectly in connection with the Services, including backups, snapshot copies, ephemeral caches (RAM, KV caches), logs that contain or can be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Data, and derivative artifacts (compiled indexes, embeddings) unless otherwise agreed.

Definitions:
- "Customer": the counterparty for whom Supplier processes data.
- "Supplier": the entity providing Services or hosting Customer Data.
- "Customer Data": any data provided to Supplier by or on behalf of Customer or generated by the Services from such data, excluding aggregated/anonymized metrics that cannot be re-identified.
- "Erase" / "Erasure": the process by which information is rendered inaccessible and unrecoverable in accordance with the Methods and Standards set out below.
- "Certification": a signed written attestation, together with supporting evidence, that Erasure has been completed per this template.

Erasure Obligations:
1) On termination or earlier written instruction from Customer, Supplier must, at Customer's election, either: (a) permanently delete and render unrecoverable all Customer Data in Supplier's possession, or (b) return all Customer Data to Customer in a common machine-readable format and then irretrievably delete Supplier copies.
2) Supplier must apply Erasure to all persistent and ephemeral storage where Customer Data resides, including backups, replicas, diagnostic dumps, KV caches, and external storage provided by third-party cloud or hosting providers that Supplier uses.
3) Supplier must ensure Erasure of embedded/derived artifacts (e.g., embeddings, indexes) that materially reproduce Customer Data where feasible; where technical infeasibility exists, Supplier must document the infeasibility and propose compensating controls for Customer review.

Methods and Standards:
- Supplier will perform Erasure using methods consistent with recognized guidance such as NIST SP 800-88 Revision 1 (Guidelines for Media Sanitization) and any relevant national standards (e.g., EU/UK guidance, ISO/IEC 27040). For cryptographically-protected data, secure destruction of cryptographic keys associated exclusively with Customer Data shall be an acceptable method where it renders the data unrecoverable.
- Logical deletion alone is insufficient for media or storage classes where data persists in backups, snapshots, or write-once archives. Supplier must follow media-appropriate sanitization steps (e.g., crypto-erase, zeroization, media destruction) dependent on storage type and provider.
- Where Customer Data exists on third-party-controlled infrastructure (e.g., cloud provider S3, block storage, managed databases), Supplier shall coordinate with the provider to achieve an effective Erasure within the provider's operational model and include provider attestations where available.

Timing and Notice:
- Supplier must commence Erasure within five (5) business days of Customer's written instruction or, in the case of termination, within the timeframe specified by the agreement (no longer than thirty (30) calendar days unless otherwise agreed).
- For data stored in long-term archives or cold storage where Erasure requires additional lead time, Supplier must notify Customer within three (3) business days with a proposed schedule and provide interim compensating controls.

Certification & Evidence:
1) Within ten (10) business days after completion of Erasure, Supplier will provide Customer a written Certification signed by an authorized security officer or engineering lead. Certification must include:
   a) A description of the scope (data types, IDs, storage locations) subject to Erasure;
   b) The methods used (including references to standards and any cryptographic key destruction performed);
   c) Dates and times when Erasure actions were executed;
   d) Any exceptions or items not Erased and the technical reasons;
   e) References to logs, snapshots, or provider attestations supporting the Erasure claim.
2) Supporting evidence must include machine-readable logs or exported manifests (redacted if necessary to protect other customers) showing the Erasure steps and outcomes, and where relevant, cryptographic key destruction receipts or proof of irreversible key deletion.
3) For higher-risk data classes (e.g., regulated personal data, healthcare, payment card), Customer may request independent verification by an agreed third party; Supplier will cooperate to schedule and provide access and will bear the cost of a single verification per 12-month period per Customer unless otherwise agreed.

Audit & Verification Rights:
- Customer will have the right to audit Supplier's compliance with the Erasure obligations, either remotely (via submitted evidence) or on-site with reasonable notice. Audits will be limited to the scope necessary to verify compliance and conducted during normal business hours.
- Supplier must not withhold access to relevant logs and artefacts on the basis that they are hosted by a third-party provider; instead Supplier must procure relevant attestations or access on Customer's behalf where direct access is not feasible.

Exceptions & Approved Retention:
- Supplier may retain copies of Customer Data to the minimum extent strictly necessary to comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes, enforce agreements, or as required by regulator; Supplier must notify Customer within five (5) business days if Supplier intends to retain data under this clause and provide the legal basis and retention period.
- Where temporary retention for forensic or incident response is necessary, Supplier must isolate retained copies, limit access to a documented list of personnel, and delete the copies within thirty (30) days of the reason ceasing unless otherwise required by law.

Remedies, Liability & Indemnity:
- If Supplier fails to perform Erasure as required, Supplier will (a) promptly remediate at Supplier's expense, (b) pay direct costs reasonably incurred by Customer to mitigate the failure (including forensic verification), and (c) be subject to available contractual damages for breach, subject to the agreement's liability provisions.
- Nothing in this clause limits Customer's rights to seek injunctive relief for failure to erase sensitive or regulated data.

Transition Assistance & Escrow of Evidence:
- Upon termination, Supplier will provide reasonable transition assistance (export formats, schema maps, export scripts) and a copy of the Erasure Certification and supporting evidence.
- Where Customer elects, Supplier will deposit a sealed, time-stamped copy of the Erasure Certification into an agreed evidence escrow (e.g., a secure document vault or third-party escrow service) and provide Customer access instructions.

Security & Operational Controls:
- Erasure processes must be executed by personnel subject to background screens and role-based access controls and must be recorded in Supplier change and release management logs.
- All Erasure operations must be performed using secure, auditable automation where practicable (e.g., scripts, orchestration tasks) and must not rely solely on manual, one-off procedures.

Definitions of Data Types & Minimal Scope Language (for insertion into Schedules):
- The parties should attach a schedule listing data categories (e.g., Production Customer Data, Test Data containing PII, Logs with PII, Derived Models/Embeddings) and the associated Erasure approach for each (immediate deletion, crypto-erase, provider attestation required, retained under legal hold).

Sample Certification Statement (to be completed by Supplier):
"I hereby certify, on behalf of [Supplier], that the Customer Data identified in the attached scope (Attachment A) has been erased or rendered irrecoverable in accordance with the Erasure Methods and Standards set forth in this template on [Date]. The attached evidence (Attachment B) documents the steps taken and supporting logs/attestations.

Authorized signatory:
Name: ___________________
Title: ____________________
Date: ____________________
"

Tailoring Notes for Negotiation:
- Parties may wish to add maximum timeframes for backups and archives specific to their cloud providers, or specify exact erasure proof formats (S3 Object Listing with delete markers, block storage zeroization proof, HSM key destruction receipts).
- Consider adding a fast-path for crypto-erase (key destruction) where architecture uses unique per-customer encryption keys (bring-your-own-key or tenant-specific keys).

Operational checklist (recommended):
- Inventory locations where Customer Data may reside (databases, caches, backups, logs).
- Identify provider-specific erasure operations and contact points.
- Prepare automation runbooks and test deprovisioning in a staging environment.
- Define evidence collection export templates and redaction rules.

Attachment placeholders: Attachment A (Scope & Data Inventory), Attachment B (Erasure Evidence Manifest).

Notes & Open Questions (for legal/engineering collaboration):
- How to handle model weights that have incorporated Customer Data via fine-tuning? (propose a separate model-provenance schedule).
- Standardized evidence formats for major cloud providers — add provider-specific examples.
- Cost allocation for third-party verification beyond the single annual check.

End of template.
